themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 24 this past week—a 419% jump from the 4.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden influx of Uber/Lyft activity or driver behavior issues in Sunnyside/Woodside that warrants investigation into what changed.
evidence: 24 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (419% spike, z-score: 8.47)
This is the 3rd-ranked spike across all complaint types by statistical significance
No prior Reddit discussion or news coverage suggests this is genuinely emerging
reporting_angles: Interview residents about specific complaints: aggressive driving, blocking sidewalks, double-parking near transit hubs
Contact TLC to determine if there's been a surge in for-hire vehicle registrations or complaints filed directly with the agency

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Problem Escalates
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks jumped to 7 complaints last week—an 833% increase from the 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—indicating a sudden spike in park-related disturbances that requires understanding whether this reflects new events, hours, or user patterns.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (833% spike, z-score: 9.45)
Ranks 2nd highest by z-score across all detected spikes
Coincides with seasonal shift or possible change in park programming/hours
reporting_angles: Survey residents near major parks (Sunnyside Park, Gantry Plaza) about what triggered the complaints
Check Parks Department records for new events, concerts, or extended hours at district parks

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Friction
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 7 last week—an 833% spike from the 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—mirroring the park noise spike and suggesting localized tension around expanded dining sheds or new restaurants in the area.
evidence: 7 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (833% spike, z-score: 4.81)
Mirrors identical complaint count (7) and spike percentage (833%) as park noise, suggesting possible geographic or timing overlap
Likely reflects strain from post-pandemic outdoor dining infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which streets or blocks are seeing the most complaints and visit to assess condition of dining sheds
Interview business owners and residents about specific friction points: noise, sidewalk obstruction, sanitation

themes_detail.label: Tree Canopy Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints reached 7 two weeks ago—a 2700% jump from the 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—representing the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting either a disease outbreak, storm damage, or systematic neglect requiring urgent Parks Department response.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2700% spike, z-score: 15.59—highest z-score in dataset)
Likely triggered by a specific event: storm damage, invasive pest, or drought stress affecting a corridor of trees
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for park upgrades, suggesting chronic underinvestment in maintenance
reporting_angles: Walk major streets (Queens Blvd, Roosevelt Ave) to document affected tree locations and visible damage
Contact Parks Department to learn what caused the spike and what remediation is underway

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints hit 28 three weeks ago—a 173% increase from the 10.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—indicating a sustained uptick in waste disposal violations that may reflect either enforcement lags or new dumping sites in the district.
evidence: 28 illegal dumping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 10.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (173% spike, z-score: 4.52)
Spike is older than the for-hire vehicle and park noise spikes, but remains statistically significant
Suggests a localized or recurring problem rather than a one-time event
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify hot spots (industrial areas, waterfront, residential blocks)
Interview Sanitation Department about enforcement actions and whether illegal dumping is tied to residential or commercial sources
